findings.title: Disclosure tests response without compelling it
findings.claim: The focus ties restraint on sign-sending to earlier denial, gives Thamud a perceptually disclosed camel that they wrong, and names fear-making as a purpose of sign-sending. Wider parallels show that even every sign may be refused, a sign could instead force submission, and fear can call recipients to caution; disclosure therefore exposes reception without guaranteeing assent. The restraint can also carry a protective or merciful reading, though that motive is not stated as exclusive.
findings.mechanism: The prevention verb in مَنَعَنَا contacts the prevention-and-precedent pattern in 18:55, while 26:4 supplies a distinct coercive-sign possibility that lets the focus's restraint carry a bounded protective extension. The qualifier مُبْصِرَةً remains open across bodily seeing, inward insight, and clarifying disclosure: 6:25 shows sight of every sign need not yield belief, 27:14 pairs sign-denial with inward certainty and wrongdoing, and 27:13 applies the same visible/clarifying form to signs dismissed as magic. The focus's sign-category also meets the 17:60 trial cue in a legacy summary and the supplied 6:25 account of continued disbelief. Finally, تخويفًا contacts 6:48's warning role and 39:16's fear-to-caution relation; ظلموا بها can be read both as boundary-crossing and, alongside 11:64-65, as a concrete violation of a protected camel-sign.
findings.reader_payoff: The sign's visibility does not settle belief: it makes the recipient's response legible. The warning can preserve room for response, while the camel's treatment exposes wrong without making every recipient respond alike.
findings.containment: The ordinary sign, visible camel, restraint, and fear-warning readings remain intact. The qualifier is not assigned one primary shade; the protective branch is a contextual extension, not a stated sole motive; the focus does not specify that the act was exactly hamstringing; and the warning is not claimed to produce caution in every recipient. The punitive reading remains live.

epistemic.reason: The cross-run publication is trusted, while the represented reader-walk and HFT summaries are legacy_unbound. Focus carriers are directly aligned; wider Arabic is supplied at ayah level without target morphology, and the 17:60 trial cue is present only as a legacy summary.

findings.title: More signs do not guarantee assent
findings.claim: The focus's repeated sign-category meets the surah's later recall of nine clear signs and Pharaoh's dismissal, while wider passages say that seeing every sign or receiving extraordinary disclosure still need not produce belief. Greater quantity therefore does not guarantee assent.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier الآيات marks signs as the recurrent object of denial and sending. In the later 17:101 connection, nine clear signs are followed by Pharaoh's dismissal; 6:25 and 6:111 extend the same response pattern to every sign and extraordinary disclosure. The repeated indicator-to-refusal relation changes the focus's restraint from a question of how much can be shown into a question of how disclosure is received.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees why a larger display need not settle a response that has already been shown to refuse signs.
findings.containment: This does not make signs pointless or claim that all recipients refuse them. It keeps the focus's stated prior-denial cause while leaving other recipients and other responses available.

findings.title: Restraint answers reception, not incapacity
findings.claim: The focus identifies earlier denial as what restrained further sign-dispatch. Wider passages affirm the ability to send a sign while withholding the demand and show that neither sworn requests nor extraordinary disclosure guarantee belief; the non-dispatch can therefore be read as a response to reception rather than scarcity or incapacity.
findings.mechanism: The carrier مَنَعَ is read both as restraint from an intended act and, in the context of 6:37, as withholding a sign that could be sent. The focus's sending verb نرسل contacts 6:37's explicit affirmation of ability, while 6:109 and 6:111 show that demands and extraordinary disclosure need not produce belief. Together, the prevention and sending carriers make non-dispatch a stated response to prior denial, not inability to act.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can distinguish a stated limit on dispatch from lack of power to send, while seeing why additional disclosure is not assumed to cure rejection.
findings.containment: The focus states prior denial as the cause in this clause; it does not claim that signs are never sent, that every demand is denied, or that the connected passages are identical events.

epistemic.reason: The HFT summary is legacy_unbound, but the focus wording, trusted cross-run publication, and supplied Arabic in 6:37, 6:109, and 6:111 independently ground the retained relation.

findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear warning as time in which a response remains possible before consequence arrives.
findings.containment: The connections support caution before consequence, not an inscribed or inevitable end and not a universal protective outcome. Punitive force remains part of the warning.

epistemic.reason: The source summary is legacy_unbound; the 39:16 and 20:134 target Arabic independently ground caution and prior opportunity, but do not support the added claim of an inscribed end.
